amendment.text: Metro does not amend the toilet-count table, the half-and-half split, rounding, the urinal rule, the small-occupancy exceptions or the single-user and all-gender provisions. Its only change to the toilet rules is one sentence added to building code Section 2902.3.4 (toilet facilities in malls): a restaurant in a mall, other than a food court tenant, must have the required facilities inside its tenant space. Metro is on the 2024 edition while the state is on 2021; the office, restaurant and school ratios, the 50/50 split, rounding up and the 50% and 67% urinal limits read the same in both. Differences in the 2024 text: the urinal limit is stated as a share of the water closets required 'for males', and a shared all-gender room needs water closet compartments (Section 405.3.4) and urinal partitions (Section 405.3.5), where the 2021 text asked for urinals in a stall or visually separated.
amendment.quote: L. Section 2902.3.4 of the 2024 Edition of the International Building Code is hereby amended by adding the following to the end of Section 2902.3.4. Restaurants other than food tenants in the food court shall have the required facilities installed within their tenant space.

quotes.urinals: In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets for males according to Table 403.1 in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets for males according to Table 403.1 in all other occupancies.
quotes.small_occupancy: Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer.
quotes.compartments: Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy.
quotes.urinal_partitions: Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy. The horizontal dimension between walls or partitions at each urinal shall be not less than 30 inches (762 mm). The walls or partitions shall begin at a height not greater than 12 inches (305 mm) from and extend not less than 60 inches (1524 mm) above the finished floor surface.

worked_examples.how: 25 women, 25 men. 25 / 25 = 1 each. Urinals may replace at most 50% of 1 = 0.5, so 0.
50 each. First 50 at 1 per 25 = 2. Urinals: 50% of 2 = 1.
100 each. First 50 at 1 per 25 = 2, remaining 50 at 1 per 50 = 1, total 3. Urinals: 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1.
200 each. First 50 = 2, remaining 150 at 1 per 50 = 3, total 5. Urinals: 50% of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
25 each. 25 / 75 = 0.33, rounded up to 1. Urinals: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so 0.
100 each. 100 / 75 = 1.33, rounded up to 2. Urinals: 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200 / 75 = 2.67, rounded up to 3. Urinals: 67% of 3 = 2.01, so 2.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Same results as the state pack: the 2024 ratios Metro enforces equal the 2021 ratios. Urinals are optional; the code does not say how the 50% and 67% limits round, and the examples round down.

Normal maintenance repairs of an existing building or structure may with the approval of the building official be made without permit, provided such repairs do not violate any provisions of this chapter. page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Nashville job sites. Price your restroom, pick the right material and see the Metro Nashville rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Nashville offices, restaurants, music venues and hospitals, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Tennessee law uses the federal access standards as its own for public buildings. Metro Nashville's building rules also apply a national accessibility standard, in its 2017 edition, and the plans are approved by the office that reviews the project.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Nashville's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Nashville sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Tennessee and federal stall rules match:** Tennessee adopted the federal standards word for word, so a stall, door or grab bar that meets one meets the other. The 2017 standard in Nashville's building rules is a separate document, so ask Metro Codes and Building Safety which sizes it checks on your project.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** under Nashville's rules a one-person restroom is marked as open to everyone. A shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and every urinal has privacy partitions. Since July 2026, state law requires shared restrooms in public colleges and universities, state prisons, juvenile detention facilities and domestic violence shelters to be designated for females, males or families. A 2021 law covers shared restrooms in public schools.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Metro Nashville requires a commercial renovation permit for renovation or maintenance work in an existing business. Its list of that work includes doors and walls and doesn't name toilet partitions. Normal maintenance repairs, such as painting and floor finishing, may be made without a permit if the building official approves. Ask Metro Codes and Building Safety (615-862-6500) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_intro: Nashville counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and every toilet needs a stall with a door. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to half of the toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, each with a privacy screen. The table shows toilets only.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. An office for 25 people or fewer, or any space for 15 or fewer, may use one shared room. Nashville adds one rule of its own: a restaurant in a mall, other than a food court tenant, must have its toilets inside its own space.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or Metro Codes and Building Safety sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Where a permit is needed, Metro Nashville issues commercial permits only to a contractor who is licensed in Tennessee, has a permit bond and holds a Metro business license. Tennessee requires a state contractor license to bid or take commercial projects of $25,000 or more. Confirm what your project needs with Metro Codes and Building Safety. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who takes out a Metro Nashville commercial permit needs a Tennessee license, a permit bond and a Metro business license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Tennessee's wage law for public work covers state highway projects only, so on a school or city building a set wage applies only where federal money brings in the federal wage rules. The federal rate for a carpenter on building work in Davidson County is $22.07 an hour, with no benefits amount listed.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 9.75% in Nashville: 7% state, 2.25% Davidson County and a 0.5% transit surcharge. The 2.75% local part applies only to the first $1,600 of the price of each single item, and the state adds 2.75% on the part of an item's price between $1,600 and $3,200.
page.buyers_extra: - **Music venues, honky-tonks and event halls:** HDPE or phenolic for restrooms that take big crowds and frequent cleaning.
